summary:
I made the three accepted review fixes to docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md and changed nothing else in the design.
- **m1:** The brief's 9-40 ms is now traced to SL-042's reflection (reflect-1.json:74), which joined SL-042's validate run (9.16-9.80 ms) and its build run (35.9-40.2 ms).
- **m2:** The Memory bullet now says "nothing is kept per folder" only of the store. It adds that the folder tree keeps the rows it built for each opened folder, in that order, until the next scan. The live-refresh item names those kept arrays as what a refresh would have to invalidate.
- **R2-m3:** The reversal is now priced against what is left of the budget: about 136 MiB of headroom on the earlier spike's layout, of which SL-042 spent 96 MiB retained (reflect-1.json:84).

I added one check to C-004 so the m1 origin sentence and its sources are asserted; it fails when the old sentence is put back. All eight cases pass.

files.why: O-011: the brief's 9-40 ms is traced to SL-042's reflection, which joined validate's 9.16-9.80 ms with the build's 35.9-40.2 ms. O-012: 'Nothing is kept per folder' is now said of the store only, and the tree's kept FolderTreeNode.Children are named in the Memory bullet and in Not covered's live-refresh item. O-013: the 136 MiB is credited to the earlier spike's throwaway layout, with SL-042's 96 MiB already spent (reflect-1.json:84).

C-004 now also checks the brief's-origin sentence and that SL-042's reflect-1.json:74 says 9-40 ms and its validate record says 9.16-9.80 ms. The old C-004 check only required '9-40' to share a line with 'brief', so it could not catch m1.

obligations.how: The sentence at docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:42-45 now reads as the accepted fix, plus the reflect-1.json:74 citation: "The slice's brief says 9-40 ms, taken from SL-042's reflection (.taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:74), which joined SL-042's validate run (9.16-9.80 ms, .taad/slices/SL-042/validate-slice-1.json) and its build run (35.9-40.2 ms). The runs above reach 44.12, so this record quotes 9-44." I checked the sources before writing it: reflect-1.json:74 says 'measured 9-40 ms against 250 ms', and validate-slice-1.json:176 says 9.16–9.80 ms. -Case C-004 now asserts both; it exits 0, and exits 1 when the old sentence is restored.

The Memory bullet now says: 'Nothing is kept per folder in the store; the folder tree keeps the rows it built for each folder it has opened, in that order, until the session ends at the next scan (src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 and :142-158)'. I checked EnsureChildren: it stores `Children = nodes` and returns early on later opens. The live-refresh item in Not covered now adds: 'The window already keeps one ordered copy: the rows the folder tree built for each folder it opened (`FolderTreeNode.Children`), which a refresh would have to invalidate.'

In the Decision section, 'paid out of the about 136 MiB of headroom SL-042's spike measured' is now 'paid out of what is left of the memory budget (the earlier spike's layout had about 136 MiB of headroom, of which SL-042 then spent 96 MiB retained, .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:84)'. That is the accepted wording, and I checked it against reflect-1.json:84 ('a throwaway layout with about 136 MiB of headroom, and this slice spent 96 MiB of retained memory').

deviations: O-012's accepted wording says the rows are kept 'until the session ends'. The doc says 'until the session ends at the next scan', because FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 says the rows are 'kept until the next scan'. The meaning is the same, tied to the code's own words.

follow_ups: Someone with access to the engine's architecture record applies the submitted find/replace in docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md (section "The engine's Scan Store line: text submitted for the edit"). This is unchanged from attempt 1.
